messages.subject: undocumented Subread behavior
messages.body_plain:
I notice that Subread 1.4.6-p1 has been released and it has this release note:

Distance between two neighboring genomic variants is allowed to be as small as 1bp (it was 16bp).

Looking at the documentation of the previous version of Subread, I see that this aspect of the aligner's algorithmic flow has not been noted in the past. I, for one, have been assuming that the aligner did not have such a requirement and have used the Subread for alignment purposes where neighboring genomic variants (mismatches) are possible (e.g., in data of cancer tissues).

It seems, then, that the aligner may have certain odd behaviors that are not documented and may be unknown to a user, and one therefore has to be careful about using Subread for identifying sequence variations (mutations in cancer, RNA editing, etc.).

Please correct me if I am wrong, and thanks again for the software which does work very well and fast for many other purposes.

messages.subject: Mapping reads longer than 1199 bp?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am currently testing the subread aligner. As I am working a lot with de
novo assemblies, where index building for each assembly Version is a
limiting step, I like your aligner, because of its fast index builder
(would it even be possible to speed index building up by using multi
cpus?).
I just tried to align long nearly error free reads which have length of
500-10000bp, but I realized that in the output bam files 1199 bp are the
Maximum length I can get! Thus subread truncates the reads. I already tried
to tweak the source code by Setting MAX_READ_LENGTH to higher values, but
nothing changed...

Could you give me some advice, what I can do to make subread work with
longer reads?

Another thing, the writing of the output files is (especially with bam output) decelerating the whole mapping speed.
Is it possible to make this multithreaded?

Thanks, Heiner
